title: Your artwork could be featured in the next Debian release
gist: Debian has opened a community artwork call for Debian 14 Forky, with a November 26 deadline. The article also notes the Toy Story naming tradition and Debian's recent milestones.

insights.claim: The Debian project is accepting community artwork for Debian 14 Forky until November 26, with art that could appear on boot screens, login prompts and wallpapers of millions of users.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Minor community news; signals Debian 14 is nearing release.
insights.locator: The Debian Linux project has opened

insights.claim: Submissions must feel distinctively Debian, integrate without patching core software and stay visually appealing over the long term, while avoiding overly busy designs that cause user fatigue.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Not investment-relevant; shows Debian's community-driven process.

insights.claim: Debian release names follow Toy Story characters; Trixie from Toy Story 3 gave Debian 13 its Ceratopsian theme by Elise Couper, and Forky from the fourth film names Debian 14.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge

insights.claim: Debian celebrated its 33rd anniversary in August 2026, released point release Trixie 13.7 on September 12, 2026, and has Forky in the later stages of development with artwork one of the final steps before release.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Debian 14 release appears close but no date is given.

insights.claim: Debian positions itself as the universal operating system, with support across different hardware architectures.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Context for its broad use in servers and embedded systems; no direct trade angle.
